subject.title: FRD: first-class multi-tenant RBAC (tenant claim on session/run/approval + tenant-scoped operator scopes + tenant-aware audit + fail-closed defaults)

question: Should OpenClaw core adopt hostile same-gateway tenant isolation as an explicit security boundary, or keep the supported model as one trusted operator boundary per Gateway?
rationale: The issue would change the documented Gateway trust model and public protocol/config behavior, so automation cannot choose the security guarantee, default posture, or migration contract.

options.title: Design core tenant isolation
options.body: Keep this FRD open and have maintainers define tenant identity propagation, scoped operator grants, audit semantics, fail-closed configuration, migration behavior, and verification requirements before implementation.

options.title: Keep isolation above Gateway
options.body: Document that downstream platforms must enforce tenant isolation before requests reach OpenClaw and continue recommending separate gateways or hosts for hostile boundaries.

options.title: Split a narrower substrate first
options.body: Defer hostile tenancy but sponsor a narrower prerequisite such as scope-aware tool policy or session envelopes without promising cross-tenant isolation.

recommendation.title: Design core tenant isolation
recommendation.body: Keep this FRD open and have maintainers define tenant identity propagation, scoped operator grants, audit semantics, fail-closed configuration, migration behavior, and verification requirements before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history around the documented Gateway trust boundary and adjacent control-plane security work.
